jobs.title: Behavioral Health Care Coordinator
jobs.description:
Finding behavioral healthcare should not require patients to understand the healthcare system before they can receive help.

Allia Health is building a clinically integrated behavioral healthcare network designed around a different standard: patients should reach the right care, at the right level, with the right combination of providers and remain connected to that care over time.

We are hiring Behavioral Health Care Coordinators to serve as the front line of that system.

Care Coordinators meet directly with individuals seeking care through Allia, understand what they are experiencing and what they need from treatment, identify appropriate providers and services across our network, and help patients move directly into care.

For some patients, that means finding the right individual clinician.

For others, it means beginning coordinated treatment with multiple specialties from the outset.
And the work does not stop once an appointment is scheduled.
Allia’s clinical technology continuously identifies potential gaps in care. Areas of focus include missed connections, disengagement, unmet referrals, and other indicators that a patient may be falling through the cracks. Our Care Coordinators respond to those signals, reconnect patients with their care teams, and help ensure that a large network of independent clinicians functions as an integrated system.

We are particularly interested in candidates with backgrounds in social work, behavioral health, case management, patient navigation, or integrated healthcare
.
This role is for someone who wants to do more than provide referrals. It is an opportunity to make sure people who need behavioral healthcare can actually find it, access it, and remain connected to care that makes sense for them.

Position Summary

The Behavioral Health Care Coordinator is a core member of Allia Health’s clinical integration infrastructure and serves as a primary point of entry for patients seeking behavioral healthcare through the Allia network.
Care Coordinators conduct structured navigation conversations with prospective patients, identify treatment needs and preferences, facilitate appropriate provider matching and scheduling, and coordinate access to multidisciplinary services when a patient’s needs extend beyond a single-provider model.
The role also provides longitudinal continuity across the network. Using information and alerts generated through Allia’s EHR and clinical intelligence infrastructure, Care Coordinators identify patients experiencing gaps in care, incomplete referrals, disengagement, access barriers, or other conditions requiring active follow-up.

The objective is straightforward but clinically important: patients should not be left to coordinate a fragmented behavioral healthcare system on their own.

Core Responsibilities

Patient Access and Navigation

Conduct phone or video-based conversations with individuals seeking care through Allia.
Develop an initial understanding of the patient’s presenting concerns, treatment goals, preferences, logistical needs, and barriers to care.
Help patients understand available treatment options without requiring them to independently navigate provider types, specialties, or systems.
Match patients with appropriate clinicians and services within the Allia network.
Schedule appointments directly when operationally available.
Facilitate timely movement from initial contact into active treatment.

Multispecialty Care Coordination

Identify situations in which a patient may benefit from more than one clinical service or specialty.
Facilitate coordinated entry into multispecialty treatment rather than relying on sequential or disconnected referrals.
Support communication and continuity between participating clinicians and practices.
Track completion of referrals and recommended services.
Ensure that care recommendations result in actual connections whenever possible.

Continuity and Patient Retention

Respond to E alerts identifying possible disruptions or gaps in care.
Follow up with patients who miss appointments, do not complete referrals, disengage unexpectedly, or experience barriers to treatment.
Work with clinicians and practices to support appropriate re-engagement.
Identify practical and systemic barriers affecting treatment access or continuity.
Escalate clinically significant concerns to appropriate members of the clinical team.

Clinical Integration

Help maintain connectivity between patients, clinicians, practices, and services across the Clinically Integrated Network.
Accurately document navigation and coordination activities.
Maintain clear boundaries between care coordination and activities requiring independent clinical judgment or licensure.
Identify recurring access, referral, and coordination problems and communicate them to clinical and operational leadership.
Participate in the continued development of Allia’s care navigation and integrated-care workflows.

Qualifications

Preferred Background

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in social work, psychology, behavioral health, human services, nursing, public health, or a related field.
MSW or comparable graduate-level behavioral health preparation strongly preferred for candidates managing more clinically complex navigation.
Experience in behavioral healthcare, case management, care coordination, patient navigation, community mental health, integrated care, or a related healthcare setting.
Social work licensure is welcomed but is not required unless responsibilities in a particular jurisdiction require it.

Required Competencies

Candidates should demonstrate:
Strong knowledge of behavioral health services and levels of care.
Ability to quickly understand patient needs while maintaining appropriate clinical boundaries.
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to establish trust remotely.
Exceptional follow-through and organizational discipline.
Ability to coordinate across multiple clinicians, practices, and systems.
Sound judgment regarding when a situation requires clinical escalation.
Comfort working with healthcare technology, clinical workflows, and data-informed alerts.
Commitment to patient access, continuity, quality, and respectful care.

What Success Looks Like

Success is not measured by the number of referrals generated.
It is measured by whether patients actually reach appropriate care.
Successful Care Coordinators help ensure that:
Patients seeking treatment move efficiently into care.
Provider matching reflects actual clinical and practical needs.
Multi-specialty treatment begins in a coordinated manner when indicated.
Referrals result in completed connections.
Care teams remain connected.
Gaps in care are recognized early.
Patients who begin to disengage do not simply disappear from the system.
Independent practices across the network operate with greater continuity than they could achieve independently.

The Care Coordinator is a critical part of Allia’s clinical safety team and of our effort to build behavioral healthcare around continuity rather than fragmentation.

We are actively hiring licensed clinicians in states specifically NY, TX, FL, NJ, MN, IL, PA, OH, GA, NC, and WA. Compensation varies by location and experience, with a salary range $65,000 to $95,000.

new_jobs.title: Behavioral Health Care Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Finding behavioral healthcare should not require patients to understand the healthcare system before they can receive help.

Allia Health is building a clinically integrated behavioral healthcare network designed around a different standard: patients should reach the right care, at the right level, with the right combination of providers and remain connected to that care over time.

We are hiring Behavioral Health Care Coordinators to serve as the front line of that system.

Care Coordinators meet directly with individuals seeking care through Allia, understand what they are experiencing and what they need from treatment, identify appropriate providers and services across our network, and help patients move directly into care.

For some patients, that means finding the right individual clinician.

For others, it means beginning coordinated treatment with multiple specialties from the outset.
And the work does not stop once an appointment is scheduled.
Allia’s clinical technology continuously identifies potential gaps in care. Areas of focus include missed connections, disengagement, unmet referrals, and other indicators that a patient may be falling through the cracks. Our Care Coordinators respond to those signals, reconnect patients with their care teams, and help ensure that a large network of independent clinicians functions as an integrated system.

We are particularly interested in candidates with backgrounds in social work, behavioral health, case management, patient navigation, or integrated healthcare
.
This role is for someone who wants to do more than provide referrals. It is an opportunity to make sure people who need behavioral healthcare can actually find it, access it, and remain connected to care that makes sense for them.

Position Summary

The Behavioral Health Care Coordinator is a core member of Allia Health’s clinical integration infrastructure and serves as a primary point of entry for patients seeking behavioral healthcare through the Allia network.
Care Coordinators conduct structured navigation conversations with prospective patients, identify treatment needs and preferences, facilitate appropriate provider matching and scheduling, and coordinate access to multidisciplinary services when a patient’s needs extend beyond a single-provider model.
The role also provides longitudinal continuity across the network. Using information and alerts generated through Allia’s EHR and clinical intelligence infrastructure, Care Coordinators identify patients experiencing gaps in care, incomplete referrals, disengagement, access barriers, or other conditions requiring active follow-up.

The objective is straightforward but clinically important: patients should not be left to coordinate a fragmented behavioral healthcare system on their own.

Core Responsibilities

Patient Access and Navigation

Conduct phone or video-based conversations with individuals seeking care through Allia.
Develop an initial understanding of the patient’s presenting concerns, treatment goals, preferences, logistical needs, and barriers to care.
Help patients understand available treatment options without requiring them to independently navigate provider types, specialties, or systems.
Match patients with appropriate clinicians and services within the Allia network.
Schedule appointments directly when operationally available.
Facilitate timely movement from initial contact into active treatment.

Multispecialty Care Coordination

Identify situations in which a patient may benefit from more than one clinical service or specialty.
Facilitate coordinated entry into multispecialty treatment rather than relying on sequential or disconnected referrals.
Support communication and continuity between participating clinicians and practices.
Track completion of referrals and recommended services.
Ensure that care recommendations result in actual connections whenever possible.

Continuity and Patient Retention

Respond to E alerts identifying possible disruptions or gaps in care.
Follow up with patients who miss appointments, do not complete referrals, disengage unexpectedly, or experience barriers to treatment.
Work with clinicians and practices to support appropriate re-engagement.
Identify practical and systemic barriers affecting treatment access or continuity.
Escalate clinically significant concerns to appropriate members of the clinical team.

Clinical Integration

Help maintain connectivity between patients, clinicians, practices, and services across the Clinically Integrated Network.
Accurately document navigation and coordination activities.
Maintain clear boundaries between care coordination and activities requiring independent clinical judgment or licensure.
Identify recurring access, referral, and coordination problems and communicate them to clinical and operational leadership.
Participate in the continued development of Allia’s care navigation and integrated-care workflows.

Qualifications

Preferred Background

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in social work, psychology, behavioral health, human services, nursing, public health, or a related field.
MSW or comparable graduate-level behavioral health preparation strongly preferred for candidates managing more clinically complex navigation.
Experience in behavioral healthcare, case management, care coordination, patient navigation, community mental health, integrated care, or a related healthcare setting.
Social work licensure is welcomed but is not required unless responsibilities in a particular jurisdiction require it.

Required Competencies

Candidates should demonstrate:
Strong knowledge of behavioral health services and levels of care.
Ability to quickly understand patient needs while maintaining appropriate clinical boundaries.
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to establish trust remotely.
Exceptional follow-through and organizational discipline.
Ability to coordinate across multiple clinicians, practices, and systems.
Sound judgment regarding when a situation requires clinical escalation.
Comfort working with healthcare technology, clinical workflows, and data-informed alerts.
Commitment to patient access, continuity, quality, and respectful care.

What Success Looks Like

Success is not measured by the number of referrals generated.
It is measured by whether patients actually reach appropriate care.
Successful Care Coordinators help ensure that:
Patients seeking treatment move efficiently into care.
Provider matching reflects actual clinical and practical needs.
Multi-specialty treatment begins in a coordinated manner when indicated.
Referrals result in completed connections.
Care teams remain connected.
Gaps in care are recognized early.
Patients who begin to disengage do not simply disappear from the system.
Independent practices across the network operate with greater continuity than they could achieve independently.

The Care Coordinator is a critical part of Allia’s clinical safety team and of our effort to build behavioral healthcare around continuity rather than fragmentation.

We are actively hiring licensed clinicians in states specifically NY, TX, FL, NJ, MN, IL, PA, OH, GA, NC, and WA. Compensation varies by location and experience, with a salary range $65,000 to $95,000.
